```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Start with `boundary_delineation()` for the predefined workflow. This guide
shows how to compare settings, inspect individual stages, and reuse a workflow
across sites. The examples illustrate software use, not recommended settings
or validated field boundaries. Remote examples are not run during the build.

```{r load-ocular}
library(ocular)
```

## Compare workflows from the same input

Retrieve scenes once and keep the resulting `rs` object:

```{r retrieve-for-stages, eval=FALSE}
rs <- get_rs(
  longitude = 147.227906,
  latitude = -33.0675167,
  start_date = "2016-05-18",
  end_date = "2016-09-21",
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-8",
  x_metres = 1000
)

field <- boundary_delineation(rs)
terra::plot(as_raster(field))
```

For a new comparison, start each run from `rs`. Here `"tight"` illustrates a
change to the calibrated matching tolerance; it is not a recommendation for
this site.

```{r compare-settings, eval=FALSE}
field_tight <- boundary_delineation(rs, strictness = "tight")
terra::plot(as_raster(field_tight))
```

Passing `field` instead reruns the workflow on its current mask. Area filling
searches within that mask using existing spectral data and fresh stage state;
later refinement stages can remove or revive cells. An empty input mask stays
empty, so return to `rs` to try another delineation.

```{r refine-current-mask, eval=FALSE}
field_refined <- boundary_delineation(field)
```

## Inspect individual stages

| Function | Role |
|---|---|
| `segment_area()` | Grows a candidate area using spectral similarity across dates. |
| `trace_perimeter()` | Removes or revives perimeter cells. Without a mask, schedules cleanup after the initial fill. |
| `segment_interior()` | Revises cells using spectral bounds and agreement with the seed signature. |
| `split_area()` | Separates adjoining areas while protecting the matching component connected to the supplied point. |

Run the stages directly when you want to inspect an intermediate result:

```{r direct-stage-chain, eval=FALSE}
candidate <- segment_area(rs)
field_manual <- candidate |>
  segment_interior() |>
  split_area() |>
  trace_perimeter()

terra::plot(as_raster(candidate))
terra::plot(as_raster(field_manual))
```

This manual chain differs from `boundary_delineation()`, which includes
repeated splitting and perimeter refinement. Its `cleanup_boundary` setting
controls additional split-and-cleanup pairs. See `?boundary_delineation` for
the sequence.

### Change settings deliberately

Settings supplied to `get_rs()` are stored on its object. Later calls can
override them without changing that stored list. In `rs_params()`, only the
settings you supply explicitly override stored or calibrated values; filled-in
defaults leave those values in place. Every entry in a plain named list is
explicit.

Leaving `area_sensitivity` unspecified allows calibrated signatures and
per-window tolerances where support is adequate. Explicitly supplying it,
even as `area_sensitivity = 0.2`, uses a scalar tolerance instead. A calibrated
fill retains eligible calibrated signatures for later refinement when learned
signatures are missing. See `?rs_params` and `?segment_area` for the full rules.

The stored parameters do not record every override supplied to later calls.
Keep the calls used for each comparison.

For example, collect perimeter settings in a list for reuse:

```{r pipeline-settings}
pipeline_params <- rs_params(
  perimeter_margins = c(0.5, 0.9),
  trace_iter = 20L
)
```

These illustrative settings leave calibrated area matching available. Low-level
controls and calibration defaults need validation for the intended use. Prefer
a small, explicit change when comparing settings; selecting particular
`search_windows` also requires those windows to exist in each input.

## Reuse a processing chain

`build_pipeline()` captures processing after retrieval. Omit the initial object
from the captured native pipe, then pass a retrieved object to the result:

```{r construct-pipeline}
time_series_pipeline <- build_pipeline(
  boundary_delineation() |>
    as_time_series(),
  params = pipeline_params
)
```

```{r run-pipeline, eval=FALSE}
vi_series <- time_series_pipeline(rs)
head(vi_series)
```

A `params` list supplied at run time replaces the captured list for that run.
Omitted settings then come from the input object and normal stage resolution.
Arguments written directly in a captured stage still take precedence.

```{r run-pipeline-override, eval=FALSE}
vi_series <- time_series_pipeline(
  rs,
  params = list(perimeter_margins = c(0.3, 0.7))
)
```

Supported stages include the four delineation functions,
`boundary_delineation()`, `add_modis()` and the output functions. Retrieval,
`add_ftw_prior()` and `validate_data_fusion()` remain separate operations.
See `?build_pipeline` for argument capture and alternative input notation.

## Process multiple sites

Give `batch_rs()` one row per site and date range, with the five columns below:

```{r batch-input}
sites <- data.frame(
  id = c("field-a", "field-b"),
  longitude = c(147.2279, 147.3150),
  latitude = c(-33.0675, -33.1010),
  start_date = "2016-05-18",
  end_date = "2016-09-21"
)
```

The default batch retrieves each site, runs `boundary_delineation()`, and
combines its time series into `id`, `index`, `source`, `date` and `value` columns.
Always inspect the per-input outcomes as well as the returned values:

```{r batch-default, eval=FALSE}
series <- batch_rs(
  sites,
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-8",
  x_metres = 1000,
  max_cloud_cover = 50
)

head(series)
attr(series, "outcomes")
attr(series, "failures")
```

`outcomes` accounts for every input row as `success`, `empty`, `failure` or
`interrupted`, with returned date counts, retrieval attempts and cache use.
An empty success contributes no time-series rows and is not a failure.
`failures` supplies reasons for failed or interrupted sites.

By default, a site has at most **three retrieval attempts**. Only classified
temporary catalogue-query or transport errors are retried. No-scenes results,
pipeline errors and asset-reading failures are final. Every retrieval attempt
uses the requested `max_cloud_cover`, including retries. `retries = Inf` allows
unlimited transient retries. Interrupting a batch
returns completed results and records unfinished sites. See `?batch_rs` for
the complete retry rules.

The batch interface accepts `max_cloud_cover`, but not `scl_classes`. For
per-pixel masking, retrieve sites individually with `get_rs()`.

### Reuse results or supply a custom pipeline

Completed results are cached by default. Repeating a matching request reuses
them; `cache = FALSE` retrieves and processes them again. Custom pipelines are
cached only when you supply `pipeline_cache_key`. Change the key whenever the
pipeline or its captured values change.

```{r batch-custom, eval=FALSE}
series <- batch_rs(
  sites,
  pipeline = time_series_pipeline,
  pipeline_cache_key = "delineation-series-v2",
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-8",
  x_metres = 1000
)
```

A custom pipeline must return `date` and one numeric `value` column. Batch
output retains these and the site/index/source labels; extra columns, including
fusion diagnostics, are discarded. The default batch maps a multi-area `union`
to `value`; a custom pipeline must make that choice itself.

## Retain disconnected areas

To keep several connected areas produced by the search, set
`multiple_areas = TRUE`. Otherwise output is limited to the centre-most area.
Here the choice is supplied to each call because it was not stored at retrieval.

```{r multiple-areas, eval=FALSE}
field_multi <- boundary_delineation(rs, multiple_areas = TRUE)
multi_raster <- as_raster(field_multi, multiple_areas = TRUE)
multi_series <- as_time_series(field_multi, multiple_areas = TRUE)

names(multi_raster)
head(multi_series)
```

When several areas remain, outputs use `area_1`, `area_2`, and so on, plus
`union`. With only one area, the ordinary single-area schema is used. These
labels identify connected output areas, not independently validated fields.

For field boundary priors and Landsat-MODIS fusion, continue to
[Experimental features](https://github.com/AAGI-AUS/ocular/blob/main/vignettes/ocular-experimental-features.Rmd).
